content_of_post_to_comment: Someone asked me “are there any problems gifted kids face as they enter adulthood?” These were my 3 knee-jerk thoughts: Burnout - feeling like they have nothing left to give, like nothing is worth it Realizing they were never taught executive functioning skills (it was assumed they had them - they didn't, they just never needed them) This overwhelming burden to be “successful" and to choose that over happiness
comment: A subtle challenge may be that gifted kids often build identity around being naturally capable. Adulthood can be jarring when effort, failure, and persistence become skills they never had to practice.
